question.text: A boat covers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> upstream and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> downstream in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>hours</mi></math> while it covers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> upstream and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> downstream in <math><mn>6</mn><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>hours</mi></math>. The velocity (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kmph</mi></math>) of the current is

solution.text:
Let rate of upstream = x kmph and rate of downstream = y kmph.

Then, 24x+36y=6….(i) and 36x+24y=132….(ii)

Solving (i) & (ii) y=12 km hr-1 and x=8 km hr-1 

∴Speed upstream = 8 kmph, Speed downstream = 12 kmph.

Hence, rate of current =1212-8 kmph = 2 kmph.
